questionText:
Consider a system of linear equations $PX = Q$ where $P \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ and $Q \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 1}$. Suppose $P$ has an LU decomposition, $P = LU$, where

$$L = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ l_{21} & 1 & 0 \\ l_{31} & l_{32} & 1 \end{bmatrix} \text{ and } U = \begin{bmatrix} u_{11} & u_{12} & u_{13} \\ 0 & u_{22} & u_{23} \\ 0 & 0 & u_{33} \end{bmatrix}.$$

Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
options: The system $PX = Q$ can be solved by first solving $LY = Q$ and then $UX = Y$.
If $P$ is invertible, then both $L$ and $U$ are invertible.
If $P$ is singular, then at least one of the diagonal elements of $U$ is zero.
If $P$ is symmetric, then both $L$ and $U$ are symmetric.
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Analysis of Option (A):
• The given system is $PX = Q$. Substituting $P = LU$ yields $(LU)X = Q \implies L(UX) = Q$.
• Letting $UX = Y$, we first solve $LY = Q$ for $Y$ using forward substitution, and then solve $UX = Y$ for $X$ using backward substitution.
• Thus, Option (A) is TRUE.

2. Analysis of Option (B):
• The determinant relation is $\det(P) = \det(L) \cdot \det(U)$.
• Since $L$ is a unit lower triangular matrix, its determinant is $\det(L) = 1 eq 0$, so $L$ is always invertible.
• If $P$ is invertible, then $\det(P) eq 0 \implies \det(U) eq 0$, which implies $U$ is also invertible.
• Thus, Option (B) is TRUE.

3. Analysis of Option (C):
• The matrix $U$ is upper triangular, so its determinant is the product of its diagonal elements: $\det(U) = u_{11} u_{22} u_{33}$.
• If $P$ is singular, $\det(P) = 0 \implies \det(L) \cdot \det(U) = 1 \cdot (u_{11} u_{22} u_{33}) = 0$.
• Therefore, at least one diagonal element $u_{ii}$ of $U$ must be zero.
• Thus, Option (C) is TRUE.

4. Analysis of Option (D):
• If $P$ is symmetric, $P = P^T \implies LU = U^T L^T$.
• This condition does not mean $L$ or $U$ are symmetric. In general, lower/upper triangular matrices are symmetric only if they are diagonal.
• For example, for $P = egin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, the LU factors are $L = egin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \ 0.5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $U = egin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \ 0 & 1.5 \end{bmatrix}$, neither of which is symmetric.
• Thus, Option (D) is FALSE.

Hence, the correct options are (A), (B), and (C).
